This struck uncomfortably deep. To be honest, at first I wasn't sure if the note was directed from one person to another, could be just as well a stream of thoughts written down. Abuse or depression? For me both can work.
I think it is one of those horrors that hide in everyday life. Thing is we don't even notice them.

On the one hand, I'm not particularly happy that you didn't like it.

On the other, it's conveying the things it's meant to convey.

You were expecting me to blame you. Why do you think so poorly of me? Why do you hate me? I am crying and it is your fault.

Yeah, like sex ed and camping in the winter. Not wiki articles.

There's absolutely a kind of enjoyment that can be derived from theoretically negative emotions — sort of an autoschadenfreude (cue linguists cringing) — but this does not evoke that. It's just an unpleasant block of gaslighting and emotional abuse.

item.content:encoded:
Tuomey, this is fantastic. I think everyone can relate to this, even people from healthy households, because it touches on something so universal that parents do without even realizing it, but it especially highlights what goes through the mind of someone who has suffered abuse. You need to write more, if this is what you're keeping from us, man.

And no, no hidden text from me.

Damn. This is such a visceral representation of emotional abuse, I started to feel like I'd done something wrong in the middle of reading it. D:

This is your fault. You made me feel this way because you hate me. This is always your fault. What if bees were your fault? You're making me mix the memes. You want me to look foolish. It is your fault. It is always your fault.
